findings.evidence: Lines 60-68 document the angle as from exit tangent to reversed entry tangent, while the code is `Complex.arg (-limUnder (𝓝[<] t₀) (deriv γ)) - Complex.arg (limUnder (𝓝[>] t₀) (deriv γ))`.
findings.fix: Swap the subtraction operands so the value is `Complex.arg (limUnder (𝓝[>] t₀) (deriv γ)) - Complex.arg (-limUnder (𝓝[<] t₀) (deriv γ))`, then normalize.
findings.issue: `crossingAngle` implements the complement of the documented/source angle for nonsmooth crossings: the doc says `arg L₊ - arg (-L₋)`, but line 68 computes `arg (-L₋) - arg L₊`.

findings.evidence: Roadmap lines 220-227 consume only `hclosed`, `hγU`, `hA`, and `hB : ConditionB γ a b f` with no endpoint avoidance, while `HasCauchyPVAt` lines 89-93 excises over the whole interval.
findings.fix: Either add the needed endpoint/basepoint condition here, or add the source-style endpoint-avoidance/reparametrization hypothesis to the consuming theorem/roadmap before claiming this predicate matches that theorem.
findings.issue: `ConditionB` only quantifies over `Set.Ioo a b` at lines 78 and 84, so a singularity at the closed curve basepoint `γ a = γ b` with no interior preimage is completely unconstrained under the roadmap theorem.

summary: The new crossing-angle primitive has the stated/source orientation reversed, and ConditionB is too weak for the roadmap theorem contract because it leaves closed-curve basepoint singularities unconstrained.
